edges.description: Increasing chip strain raised baseline apparent permeability slightly and, after infection, increased vascular bacterial counts and permeability. edges.limitations: The uniform chip deformation does not reproduce regional overdistension and recruitment-derecruitment in an injured lung. There are no seeded immune cells. edges.description: Infection plus greater chip strain increased apparent permeability and vascular-channel bacterial counts. These readouts model aspects of barrier dysfunction without reproducing the full syndrome.
edges.limitations: Barrier failure is measured as apparent permeability and bacterial translocation over 12 hours, without the protein-rich alveolar flooding, coagulation, or leukocyte transmigration that accompany the lesion clinically.

edges.description: Increasing cyclic strain from 5% to 10% modulates IL-6 and IL-8 release in the infected chip. Cytokine levels decrease under greater strain despite increased barrier injury.
edges.limitations: This comparison measures cytokine output in an epithelial-endothelial chip without seeded immune cells at 12 hours after infection. It does not establish a clinical anti-inflammatory benefit of greater ventilation strain.

evidence.snippet: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a clinical syndrome of acute hypoxemic respiratory failure due to lung inflammation, not caused by cardiogenic pulmonary edema.

nodes.description: Conditional recommendation for higher PEEP without recruitment maneuvers in moderate-to-severe adult ARDS. Prolonged recruitment (PEEP ≥35 cm H2O for >60 seconds) is strongly discouraged. Titrate with respiratory and hemodynamic monitoring; mild ARDS does not inherit this recommendation. ESICM found insufficient evidence to recommend routine higher versus lower PEEP/FiO2 titration for mortality across all ARDS. The ATS conditional recommendation is restricted to moderate-to-severe disease.

nodes.description: Conditional recommendation, low certainty, for early (<48 hours) severe ARDS (PaO2/FiO2 ≤100). Use selectively when deep sedation is already required or persistent dyssynchrony compromises protection. Limit duration to 48 hours when possible; mortality advantage was not established against light sedation. ESICM 2023 recommends against routine continuous infusions for mortality reduction in unselected moderate-to-severe non-COVID ARDS; this differs in scope from ATS selective early severe use. ICU-acquired weakness and sedation harms matter.

nodes.description: Inflammatory activation can shift cellular metabolism toward glycolysis. Its magnitude and persistence vary by cell type and compartment; a uniform glycolysis-dominant state is not established in every patient with ARDS.

evidence.reference_title: Immunometabolic reprogramming and mitochondrial dysfunction in acute respiratory distress syndrome: mechanisms, metabolic resilience, and therapeutic perspectives- a narrative review.
evidence.snippet: When macrophages encounter inflammatory stimuli, they shift from mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation to aerobic glycolysis, a phenomenon called as the “Warburg effect.” This metabolic transition enables rapid ATP generation and provides biosynthetic intermediates required for cytokine production and effector functions.

nodes.description: Chlorine is among the commonest chemical causes of acute lung injury, encountered through transport accidents, industrial spills, water treatment and swimming-pool exposures, and deliberate release. Inhaled chlorine reacts in the airway to form oxidative products, so the insult delivered to the alveolar-capillary interface is chemical and oxidative rather than infectious or mechanical.

nodes.description: Nebulized recombinant human GM-CSF (molgramostim) administered as host-directed therapy to promote alveolar macrophage activation and restoration of barrier function. A phase 2a trial investigated safety, feasibility, and efficacy of low-dose (150 μg) or high-dose (450 μg) administration for 3 days in pneumonia-related ARDS. While the primary composite outcome did not reach significance, high-dose treatment showed beneficial secondary outcomes including upregulation of CD206 on alveolar macrophages (significant against both placebo and low dose; HLA-DR upregulation was significant only against low dose), improved oxygenation, and decreased SOFA scores without increasing alveolar or systemic inflammation.

evidence.reference_title: Inhaled granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (molgramostim) as host-directed therapy for pneumonia-related acute respiratory distress syndrome: a multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled phase 2a trial (GI-HOPE).
evidence.snippet: high-dose rhGM-CSF treatment revealed a favourable profile of oxygenation at the end of analysis compared to time-points before inhalation (p=0.095 and p=0.0175) or compared to the low-dose and placebo groups (p=0.0063 and p=0.0198; visit 13), and was associated with decreased SOFA scores in the high-dose group over time (p=0.0013 and p=0.00023 compared to low dose and placebo).

nodes.description: Smoke inhalation exposes the respiratory tract to toxic gases and particles that can injure distal lung and impair surfactant. Thermal injury primarily affects the upper airway; it is not treated as the alveolar mechanism. ARDS may coexist with cutaneous burns and other fire-related injuries.

evidence.reference_title: Preclinical and clinical studies of smoke-inhalation-induced acute lung injury: update on both pathogenesis and innovative therapy.
evidence.snippet: Approximately 22% of all burn patients are diagnosed with SI-ALI, leading to at least 30% of the overall fire-associated mortality.

nodes.description: Alveolar epithelial injury and the protein-rich edema environment impair the surface-tension-lowering function of surfactant.

evidence.reference_title: Acute respiratory distress syndrome.
evidence.snippet: In addition, the many biological changes resulting from both endothelial and epithelial injury, and culminating in protein-rich oedematous fluid, contribute to surfactant dysfunction90.

nodes.description: An elevated respiratory rate is a clinical sign of acute respiratory distress.

evidence.reference_title: Acute respiratory distress syndrome.
evidence.snippet: On physical examination, they appear to be in moderate or severe respiratory distress with an elevated respiratory rate and tachycardia and they usually are working harder than normal to breathe.

nodes.description: Excessive tidal deformation, overdistension and repeated opening and closure can amplify epithelial and endothelial injury in the reduced aerated lung. Exposure depends on ventilator settings, lung mechanics and patient effort.

evidence.reference_title: Acute respiratory distress syndrome.
evidence.snippet: High tidal volume and elevated airway pressure induce biomechanical inflammatory injury and necrosis of the lung endothelium and alveolar epithelium that are associated with release of neutrophil products, including proteases, oxidants and pro-inflammatory cytokines, and a reduction in the capacity of the alveolar epithelium to remove oedematous fluid36,95,96.

experimental_models.description: Increasing chip strain raised baseline apparent permeability slightly and, after infection, increased vascular bacterial counts and permeability. This demonstrates a mechanical-infectious interaction in this cell system without establishing the size of a clinical ventilation effect.
experimental_models.name: Organoid-derived Pseudomonas pneumonia-on-a-chip (VAP) model
